title: Strictification of a normal crossings boundary
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field and $V$ an integral regular finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Z\subset V$ be a normal crossings effective Cartier divisor [def-weil-closed-immersion]: etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism] at every point it is cut out by a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters. The empty divisor is allowed, and global components of $Z$ are allowed to have self-intersections. Then there is an integral smooth finite-type $F$-scheme $V_2$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and a proper $F$-morphism $q:V_2\to V$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], isomorphic over $V\setminus|Z|$ with dense inverse image of that open, such that $Z_2=(q^{-1}Z)_{\rm red}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is a strict normal crossings divisor. Explicitly $Z_2$ is a reduced effective Cartier divisor with finitely many smooth irreducible components whose intersection for any $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth of codimension $r$ in $V_2$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 4.1.2--4.1.8, printed pp. 117--118: permissible blowups and Step 2 (strictification by maximal-multiplicity strata). The passage from regular strata to smooth strata over an algebraically closed field is Stacks 0B8X, varieties.tex, lemma-dense-smooth-open-variety-over-perfect-field; the normal-crossings intersection criterion is also explained in VIII, Remark 4.2.2(i).

proof.text: The field spectrum is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $V$ Noetherian. Put $U=V\setminus|Z|$. The effective Cartier condition means the ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. By [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-nowhere-dense], $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense, in particular dense and nonempty since $V$ is integral. It is quasi-compact because $V$ is Noetherian. These facts apply also to $Z=\varnothing$, when $U=V$.

source.place: VIII 4.1.1--4.1.2, preliminary hypotheses for the permissible tower; Stacks 01T6 and 07ZU.

proof.text: Set $X_0=V$, $D_0=B_0=Z$ and $H_0=\varnothing$. We construct $q_i:X_i\to V$ inductively with $X_i$ integral regular Noetherian and finite type over $F$, $q_i^{-1}U\cong U$ scheme-theoretically dense, $D_i$ the strict transform of the original divisor, $B_i=(q_i^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$ normal crossings, and $H_i$ strict normal crossings with $B_i=D_i\cup H_i$. Both $D_i$ and $H_i$ are reduced unions of components of $B_i$. These assertions hold at $i=0$ by the hypotheses and step 1. If $D_0\ne\varnothing$, [lem-trf-nc-maximal-branch-blowup] supplies its finite maximum branch number $d$; otherwise put $d=0$ and perform no blowup.

source.place: VIII 4.1.3 and 4.1.6, initial boundary, its strict transform, accumulated exceptional divisor and depth.

proof.text: If $D_i\ne\varnothing$, apply [lem-trf-nc-maximal-branch-blowup] to $(X_i,B_i,D_i)$. Let $m_i$ be its maximum branch number and $M_i$ the reduced locus attaining it. This is a regular closed center contained in $D_i\subset B_i$, and its parameters are part of the parameters for $B_i$. Blow it up: $b_i:X_{i+1}\to X_i$. The strict transform $D_{i+1}$ has branch number at most $m_i-1$. The ideal of the closed center is of finite type because $X_i$ is Noetherian, so [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper] makes $b_i$ proper. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] it is an isomorphism over the complement of $M_i$, hence over $q_i^{-1}U$. Properness includes finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] ensure that $X_{i+1}$ is again finite type over $F$ and Noetherian.

source.place: VIII 4.1.6--4.1.8; the properness and complement properties of blowups.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-permissible-boundary-preservation] with $B=B_i$, $H=H_i$ and $M=M_i$. Its coordinate-center condition is exactly the conclusion of step 3. It gives regular $X_{i+1}$, normal crossings $B_{i+1}=(b_i^{-1}B_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and strict normal crossings $H_{i+1}=(b_i^{-1}(H_i\cup M_i))_{\mathrm{red}}$. If $E_{i+1}=(b_i^{-1}M_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$, its two strict-transform identities give $B_{i+1}=B_i^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E_{i+1}$ and $H_{i+1}=H_i^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E_{i+1}$. Taking closures of the finite union $B_i=D_i\cup H_i$ after removing $M_i$ gives $B_i^{\mathrm{st}}=D_{i+1}\cup H_i^{\mathrm{st}}$; thus $B_{i+1}=D_{i+1}\cup H_{i+1}$. These are equalities of reduced closed subschemes, since all have the indicated closed support [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Each remaining branch of $D_{i+1}$ is consequently a branch of $B_{i+1}$, as required for the next application.

source.place: VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), Lemma 4.2.9, and the induction of 4.1.8.

proof.text: Use [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-preserves-density] with the quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open $q_i^{-1}U$; the center is disjoint from this open by step 3. The open $q_{i+1}^{-1}U\cong U$ is therefore scheme-theoretically dense in $X_{i+1}$. This also verifies integrality without assuming it for a blowup: the closure of the nonempty irreducible open $U$ is all of $X_{i+1}$, so its space is irreducible. Any nilpotent local section restricts to zero on the reduced open $U$, and is zero by the injectivity defining scheme-theoretic density. Hence $X_{i+1}$ is reduced and irreducible, that is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. This completes all the induction invariants.

source.place: VIII 4.1.3--4.1.8, admissibility of the tower and preservation of the dense open.

proof.text: As long as $D_i\ne\varnothing$, step 3 gives $m_{i+1}\leq m_i-1$ if $D_{i+1}$ is nonempty. Since a nonempty divisor has at least one branch at one geometric point, the process stops with $D_N=\varnothing$ after at most $d$ steps. The case $m_i=1$ is included: $M_i=D_i$ is a Cartier divisor, its blowup may be an identity morphism, but the strict transform of $D_i$ is empty because its complement in $D_i$ outside the center is empty. Step 4 therefore gives $B_N=H_N$. The SNC assertion for $H_N$ includes finitely many regular irreducible components and regular codimension-$r$ intersections, by [lem-trf-permissible-boundary-preservation]; if $N=0$ the boundary is empty and these assertions are vacuous.

source.place: VIII 4.1.7--4.1.8: termination, including the final codimension-one blowup.

proof.text: Put $V_2=X_N$ and $q=q_N=b_0\circ\cdots\circ b_{N-1}$. The finite composite is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] (for $N=0$, the identity is proper directly from the definition). It is an $F$-morphism and is an isomorphism over $U$, with dense inverse image, by the induction. Reduction does not change supports [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], and inverse images of sets compose, so the recurrence $B_{i+1}=(b_i^{-1}B_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$ identifies $B_N$ with $(q^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Integrality, regularity and finite type of $V_2$ have already been checked.

source.place: VIII 4.1.8, conclusion for the composite permissible tower.

proof.text: An algebraically closed field $F$ is perfect: in positive characteristic every element has a $p$th root, and in characteristic zero fields are perfect. Apply [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] to the regular finite-type $F$-scheme $V_2$ to obtain smoothness. Each component of $B_N$ and each nonempty intersection of distinct components is regular by step 6 and is locally of finite type over $F$: on an affine chart its coordinate ring is a quotient of a finitely generated $F$-algebra, generated by the images of the same generators [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Applying the same lemma to each such closed subscheme makes it smooth over $F$, without changing its codimension. Together with the reduced Cartier assertion of step 6 this is exactly the required explicit strict normal crossings conclusion, including the empty divisor.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.8, printed pp. 117--118; Lemma 4.2.9 and Remark 4.2.2(i); final regular-to-smooth passage is Stacks 0B8X.

Two new single-step geometric lemmas separate the depth drop from permissible boundary preservation. A third general regular-to-smooth node has an exact sorry-free slopmaster2 attachment candidate. lean.statement: theorem exists_normalCrossings_strictification (F : Type u) [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (V : Scheme.{u}) (f : V ⟶ Spec (.of F)) [IsIntegral V] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (hV : ∀ x : V, ∃ U : V.affineOpens, x ∈ U.1 ∧ IsRegularRing Γ(V, U.1)) (Z : V.IdealSheafData) (hZ : Z.IsNormalCrossingsDivisor) : ∃ (V₂ : Scheme.{u}) (f₂ : V₂ ⟶ Spec (.of F)) (q : V₂ ⟶ V), IsIntegral V₂ ∧ Smooth f₂ ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType f₂ ∧ QuasiCompact f₂ ∧ q ≫ f = f₂ ∧ IsProper q ∧ IsIso (q ∣_ Z.support.compl) ∧ Dense ((q ⁻¹ᵁ Z.support.compl : V₂.Opens) : Set V₂) ∧ ((Z.comap q).radical).IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor f₂
